title: Government calamity spending surges 35% at end-August as disasters strike
summary: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction…

blocks.text: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction requirements nationwide.

Data from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) showed that cumulative end-August releases jumped by 35.3 percent from the end-July total of ₱10.4 billion. As of Aug. 31, the available balance of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) stood at ₱26.1 billion.

This total is drawn from a ₱40.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2026—consisting of ₱23.5 billion for the NDRRM Program (NDRRMP), ₱15.3 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program (DRRAP) for local government units, and ₱1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund (PSF)—supplemented by ₱322.9 million in continuing appropriations from 2025.

To date, all disbursements have been sourced exclusively from the NDRRMP. The bulk, totaling ₱12.9 billion, was directed toward Quick Response Fund (QRF) augmentations for immediate relief and rehabilitation. Meanwhile, ₱1.1 billion was released for specific rehabilitation and logistics projects approved by the Office of the President (OP).
While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) was previously the sole recipient of QRF augmentations, several other national agencies have now received standby funds.

The DSWD remains the largest recipient, drawing ₱11.4 billion in total QRF replenishments across six tranches: ₱2 billion in February, ₱1.9 billion in March, ₱2 billion in April, ₱1.7 billion in June, ₱2 billion in July, and ₱1.8 billion in August.
Among other agencies receiving emergency funds, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) received ₱1.2 billion in August for its first QRF replenishment of the year.

The Department of National Defense (DND) received ₱300 million in July for the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) QRF, while the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) received ₱50 million in July for the Philippine National Police (PNP) QRF.

Apart from emergency relief, the ₱1.1 billion approved by the OP for targeted resilience projects includes ₱650 million for the DPWH to retrofit and strengthen the San Juanico Bridge in Region VIII, ₱385.1 million for the DND-OCD’s NDRRMC Integrated Logistics Hub at Lumbia Airport, and ₱44.8 million for DSWD command center repairs in Clark and rescue vehicle procurement.

Following these releases, the NDRRMP holds an available balance of ₱9.5 billion. When combined with the untouched DRRAP at ₱15.3 billion and the total PSF at ₱1.3 billion, the government retains ₱26.1 billion to address disaster-related and climate-mitigation requirements for the remaining four months of the year.
